From cgraphs.locks.lambdalock Require Export langdef.

Fixpoint expr_refs e :=
  match e with
  | Val v => val_refs v
  | Var x => ∅
  | Fun x e => expr_refs e
  | App e1 e2 => expr_refs e1 ∪ expr_refs e2
  | Unit => ∅
  | Pair e1 e2 => expr_refs e1 ∪ expr_refs e2
  | LetPair e1 e2 => expr_refs e1 ∪ expr_refs e2
  | Sum i e => expr_refs e
  | MatchSum n e es => expr_refs e ∪ fin_union n (expr_refs ∘ es)
  | ForkBarrier e => expr_refs e
  | NewLock e => expr_refs e
  | ForkLock e1 e2 => expr_refs e1 ∪ expr_refs e2
  | Acquire e => expr_refs e
  | Release e1 e2 => expr_refs e1 ∪ expr_refs e2
  | Wait e => expr_refs e
  | Drop e => expr_refs e
  end
with val_refs v :=
  match v with
  | FunV x e => expr_refs e
  | UnitV => ∅
  | PairV v1 v2 => val_refs v1 ∪ val_refs v2
  | SumV i v => val_refs v
  | BarrierV i => {[ i ]}
  | LockV i => {[ i ]}
  end.

Definition obj_refs x :=
  match x with
  | Thread e => expr_refs e
  | Barrier => ∅
  | Lock refcnt o =>
      match o with
      | Some v => val_refs v
      | None => ∅
      end
  end.

Inductive expr_head_waiting : expr -> nat -> Prop :=
  | Barrier_waiting j v :
    expr_head_waiting (App (Val $ BarrierV j) (Val v)) j
  | ForkLock_waiting j v :
    expr_head_waiting (ForkLock (Val $ LockV j) (Val v)) j
  | Acquire_waiting j :
    expr_head_waiting (Acquire (Val $ LockV j)) j
  | Release_waiting j v :
    expr_head_waiting (Release (Val $ LockV j) (Val v)) j
  | Wait_waiting j :
    expr_head_waiting (Wait (Val $ LockV j)) j
  | Drop_waiting j :
    expr_head_waiting (Drop (Val $ LockV j)) j.

Definition expr_waiting e j :=
  ∃ k e', ctx k ∧ e = k e' ∧ expr_head_waiting e' j.

Definition waiting (ρ : cfg) (i j : nat) :=
  (∃ e, ρ !! i = Some (Thread e) ∧ expr_waiting e j) ∨
  (∃ y, ρ !! j = Some y ∧ i ∈ obj_refs y ∧ ∀ e, y = Thread e -> ¬ expr_waiting e i).

Definition can_step (ρ : cfg) (i : nat) := ∃ ρ', step i ρ ρ'.

Definition inactive (ρ : cfg) (i : nat) := ρ !! i = None.

Inductive reachable (ρ : cfg) : nat -> Prop :=
  | Can_step_reachable i :
      can_step ρ i -> reachable ρ i
  | Waiting_reachable i j :
      waiting ρ i j -> reachable ρ j -> reachable ρ i.

Definition fully_reachable (ρ : cfg) :=
  ∀ i, inactive ρ i ∨ reachable ρ i.

1	From Stdlib Require Import Strings.String.
2	From stdpp Require Import gmap.
3	
4	From cgraphs.locks.lambdalock Require Export langtools.
5	
6	Inductive expr :=
7	  | Val : val -> expr
8	  | Var : string -> expr
9	  | Fun : string -> expr -> expr
10	  | App : expr -> expr -> expr
11	  | Unit : expr
12	  | Pair : expr -> expr -> expr
13	  | LetPair : expr -> expr -> expr
14	  | Sum : nat -> expr -> expr
15	  | MatchSum n : expr -> (fin n -> expr) -> expr
16	
17	  | ForkBarrier : expr -> expr
18	
19	  | NewLock : expr -> expr
20	  | ForkLock : expr -> expr -> expr
21	  | Acquire : expr -> expr
22	  | Release : expr -> expr -> expr
23	  | Wait : expr -> expr
24	  | Drop : expr -> expr
25	with val :=
26	  | FunV : string -> expr -> val
27	  | UnitV : val
28	  | PairV : val -> val -> val
29	  | SumV : nat -> val -> val
30	  | BarrierV : nat -> val
31	  | LockV : nat -> val.
32	
33	Inductive linearity := Lin | Unr.
34	
35	Inductive lockstate := Opened | Closed.
36	
37	Inductive lockownership := Owner | Client.
38	
39	Definition lockcap : Type := lockownership * lockstate.
40	
41	Inductive lockownership_split : lockownership -> lockownership -> lockownership -> Prop :=
42	  | lo_split_1 : lockownership_split Owner Client Owner
43	  | lo_split_2 : lockownership_split Owner Owner Client
44	  | lo_split_3 : lockownership_split Client Client Client.
45	
46	Inductive lockstate_split : lockstate -> lockstate -> lockstate -> Prop :=
47	  | ls_split_1 : lockstate_split Opened Closed Opened
48	  | ls_split_2 : lockstate_split Opened Opened Closed
49	  | ls_split_3 : lockstate_split Closed Closed Closed.
50	
51	Definition lockcap_split l1 l2 l3 :=
52	  lockownership_split l1.1 l2.1 l3.1 ∧ lockstate_split l1.2 l2.2 l3.2.
53	
54	CoInductive type :=
55	  | FunT : linearity -> type -> type -> type
56	  | UnitT : type
57	  | PairT : type -> type -> type
58	  | SumT n : (fin n -> type) -> type
59	  | LockT : lockcap -> type -> type.
60	
61	CoInductive unr : type -> Prop :=
62	  | Fun_unr t1 t2 : unr (FunT Unr t1 t2)
63	  | Unit_unr : unr UnitT
64	  | Pair_unr t1 t2 : unr t1 -> unr t2 -> unr (PairT t1 t2)
65	  | Sum_unr n ts : (∀ i, unr (ts i)) -> unr (SumT n ts).
66	
67	Definition env := gmap string type.
68	
69	Definition env_unr (Γ : env) :=
70	  ∀ x t, Γ !! x = Some t -> unr t.
71	
72	Definition disj (Γ1 Γ2 : env) :=
73	  ∀ i t1 t2, Γ1 !! i = Some t1 -> Γ2 !! i = Some t2 -> t1 = t2 ∧ unr t1.
74	
75	Definition env_split (Γ : env) (Γ1 : env) (Γ2 : env) :=
76	  Γ = Γ1 ∪ Γ2 ∧ disj Γ1 Γ2.
77	
78	Definition env_bind (Γ' : env) (x : string) (t : type) (Γ : env) :=
79	  Γ' = <[ x := t ]> Γ ∧ ∀ t', Γ !! x = Some t' -> unr t'.
80	
81	Definition env_var (Γ : env) (x : string) (t : type) :=
82	  ∃ Γ', Γ = <[ x := t ]> Γ' ∧ env_unr Γ'.
83	
84	Inductive typed : env -> expr -> type -> Prop :=
85	
86	  | Var_typed Γ x t :
87	    env_var Γ x t ->
88	    typed Γ (Var x) t
89	  | Fun_typed Γ Γ' x e t1 t2 l :
90	    env_bind Γ' x t1 Γ ->
91	    (l = Unr -> env_unr Γ) ->
92	    typed Γ' e t2 ->
93	    typed Γ (Fun x e) (FunT l t1 t2)
94	  | App_typed Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t1 t2 l :
95	    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
96	    typed Γ1 e1 (FunT l t1 t2) ->
97	    typed Γ2 e2 t1 ->
98	    typed Γ (App e1 e2) t2
99	  | Unit_typed Γ :
100	    env_unr Γ ->
101	    typed Γ Unit UnitT
102	  | Pair_typed Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t1 t2 :
103	    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
104	    typed Γ1 e1 t1 ->
105	    typed Γ2 e2 t2 ->
106	    typed Γ (Pair e1 e2) (PairT t1 t2)
107	  | LetPair_typed Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t1 t2 t :
108	    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
109	    typed Γ1 e1 (PairT t1 t2) ->
110	    typed Γ2 e2 (FunT Lin t1 (FunT Lin t2 t)) ->
111	    typed Γ (LetPair e1 e2) t
112	  | Sum_typed Γ n (ts : fin n -> type) i e :
113	    typed Γ e (ts i) ->
114	    typed Γ (Sum i e) (SumT n ts)
115	  | MatchSumN_typed n Γ Γ1 Γ2 t (ts : fin n -> type) es e :
116	    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
117	    (n = 0 -> env_unr Γ2) ->
118	    typed Γ1 e (SumT n ts) ->
119	    (∀ i, typed Γ2 (es i) (FunT Lin (ts i) t)) ->
120	    typed Γ (MatchSum n e es) t
121	
122	  | Fork_typed Γ e t1 t2 :
123	    typed Γ e (FunT Lin (FunT Lin t2 t1) UnitT) ->
124	    typed Γ (ForkBarrier e) (FunT Lin t1 t2)
125	
126	  | NewLock_typed Γ e t :
127	    typed Γ e t ->
128	    typed Γ (NewLock e) (LockT (Owner,Closed) t)
129	  | ForkLock_typed Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t l1 l2 l3 :
130	    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
131	    lockcap_split l1 l2 l3 ->
132	    typed Γ1 e1 (LockT l1 t) ->
133	    typed Γ2 e2 (FunT Lin (LockT l2 t) UnitT) ->
134	    typed Γ (ForkLock e1 e2) (LockT l3 t)
135	  | Acquire_typed Γ e t lo :
136	    typed Γ e (LockT (lo,Closed) t) ->
137	    typed Γ (Acquire e) (PairT (LockT (lo,Opened) t) t)
138	  | Release_typed Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t lo :
139	    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
140	    typed Γ1 e1 (LockT (lo,Opened) t) ->
141	    typed Γ2 e2 t ->
142	    typed Γ (Release e1 e2) (LockT (lo,Closed) t)

From Stdlib Require Import Strings.String.
From stdpp Require Import gmap.

From cgraphs.locks.lambdalock Require Export langtools.

Inductive expr :=
  | Val : val -> expr
  | Var : string -> expr
  | Fun : string -> expr -> expr
  | App : expr -> expr -> expr
  | Unit : expr
  | Pair : expr -> expr -> expr
  | LetPair : expr -> expr -> expr
  | Sum : nat -> expr -> expr
  | MatchSum n : expr -> (fin n -> expr) -> expr

  | ForkBarrier : expr -> expr

  | NewLock : expr -> expr
  | ForkLock : expr -> expr -> expr
  | Acquire : expr -> expr
  | Release : expr -> expr -> expr
  | Wait : expr -> expr
  | Drop : expr -> expr
with val :=
  | FunV : string -> expr -> val
  | UnitV : val
  | PairV : val -> val -> val
  | SumV : nat -> val -> val
  | BarrierV : nat -> val
  | LockV : nat -> val.

Inductive linearity := Lin | Unr.

Inductive lockstate := Opened | Closed.

Inductive lockownership := Owner | Client.

Definition lockcap : Type := lockownership * lockstate.

Inductive lockownership_split : lockownership -> lockownership -> lockownership -> Prop :=
  | lo_split_1 : lockownership_split Owner Client Owner
  | lo_split_2 : lockownership_split Owner Owner Client
  | lo_split_3 : lockownership_split Client Client Client.

Inductive lockstate_split : lockstate -> lockstate -> lockstate -> Prop :=
  | ls_split_1 : lockstate_split Opened Closed Opened
  | ls_split_2 : lockstate_split Opened Opened Closed
  | ls_split_3 : lockstate_split Closed Closed Closed.

Definition lockcap_split l1 l2 l3 :=
  lockownership_split l1.1 l2.1 l3.1 ∧ lockstate_split l1.2 l2.2 l3.2.

CoInductive type :=
  | FunT : linearity -> type -> type -> type
  | UnitT : type
  | PairT : type -> type -> type
  | SumT n : (fin n -> type) -> type
  | LockT : lockcap -> type -> type.

CoInductive unr : type -> Prop :=
  | Fun_unr t1 t2 : unr (FunT Unr t1 t2)
  | Unit_unr : unr UnitT
  | Pair_unr t1 t2 : unr t1 -> unr t2 -> unr (PairT t1 t2)
  | Sum_unr n ts : (∀ i, unr (ts i)) -> unr (SumT n ts).

Definition env := gmap string type.

Definition env_unr (Γ : env) :=
  ∀ x t, Γ !! x = Some t -> unr t.

Definition disj (Γ1 Γ2 : env) :=
  ∀ i t1 t2, Γ1 !! i = Some t1 -> Γ2 !! i = Some t2 -> t1 = t2 ∧ unr t1.

Definition env_split (Γ : env) (Γ1 : env) (Γ2 : env) :=
  Γ = Γ1 ∪ Γ2 ∧ disj Γ1 Γ2.

Definition env_bind (Γ' : env) (x : string) (t : type) (Γ : env) :=
  Γ' = <[ x := t ]> Γ ∧ ∀ t', Γ !! x = Some t' -> unr t'.

Definition env_var (Γ : env) (x : string) (t : type) :=
  ∃ Γ', Γ = <[ x := t ]> Γ' ∧ env_unr Γ'.

Inductive typed : env -> expr -> type -> Prop :=

  | Var_typed Γ x t :
    env_var Γ x t ->
    typed Γ (Var x) t
  | Fun_typed Γ Γ' x e t1 t2 l :
    env_bind Γ' x t1 Γ ->
    (l = Unr -> env_unr Γ) ->
    typed Γ' e t2 ->
    typed Γ (Fun x e) (FunT l t1 t2)
  | App_typed Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t1 t2 l :
    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
    typed Γ1 e1 (FunT l t1 t2) ->
    typed Γ2 e2 t1 ->
    typed Γ (App e1 e2) t2
  | Unit_typed Γ :
    env_unr Γ ->
    typed Γ Unit UnitT
  | Pair_typed Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t1 t2 :
    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
    typed Γ1 e1 t1 ->
    typed Γ2 e2 t2 ->
    typed Γ (Pair e1 e2) (PairT t1 t2)
  | LetPair_typed Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t1 t2 t :
    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
    typed Γ1 e1 (PairT t1 t2) ->
    typed Γ2 e2 (FunT Lin t1 (FunT Lin t2 t)) ->
    typed Γ (LetPair e1 e2) t
  | Sum_typed Γ n (ts : fin n -> type) i e :
    typed Γ e (ts i) ->
    typed Γ (Sum i e) (SumT n ts)
  | MatchSumN_typed n Γ Γ1 Γ2 t (ts : fin n -> type) es e :
    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
    (n = 0 -> env_unr Γ2) ->
    typed Γ1 e (SumT n ts) ->
    (∀ i, typed Γ2 (es i) (FunT Lin (ts i) t)) ->
    typed Γ (MatchSum n e es) t

  | Fork_typed Γ e t1 t2 :
    typed Γ e (FunT Lin (FunT Lin t2 t1) UnitT) ->
    typed Γ (ForkBarrier e) (FunT Lin t1 t2)

  | NewLock_typed Γ e t :
    typed Γ e t ->
    typed Γ (NewLock e) (LockT (Owner,Closed) t)
  | ForkLock_typed Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t l1 l2 l3 :
    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
    lockcap_split l1 l2 l3 ->
    typed Γ1 e1 (LockT l1 t) ->
    typed Γ2 e2 (FunT Lin (LockT l2 t) UnitT) ->
    typed Γ (ForkLock e1 e2) (LockT l3 t)
  | Acquire_typed Γ e t lo :
    typed Γ e (LockT (lo,Closed) t) ->
    typed Γ (Acquire e) (PairT (LockT (lo,Opened) t) t)
  | Release_typed Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t lo :
    env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
    typed Γ1 e1 (LockT (lo,Opened) t) ->
    typed Γ2 e2 t ->
    typed Γ (Release e1 e2) (LockT (lo,Closed) t)
  | Wait_typed Γ e t :
    typed Γ e (LockT (Owner,Closed) t) ->
    typed Γ (Wait e) t
  | Drop_typed Γ e t :
    typed Γ e (LockT (Client,Closed) t) ->
    typed Γ (Drop e) UnitT.

Definition subst (x:string) (a:val) := fix rec e :=
  match e with
  | Val _ => e
  | Var x' => if decide (x = x') then Val a else e
  | Fun x' e => Fun x' (if decide (x = x') then e else rec e)
  | App e1 e2 => App (rec e1) (rec e2)
  | Unit => Unit
  | Pair e1 e2 => Pair (rec e1) (rec e2)
  | LetPair e1 e2 => LetPair (rec e1) (rec e2)
  | Sum n e => Sum n (rec e)
  | MatchSum n e1 e2 => MatchSum n (rec e1) (rec ∘ e2)
  | ForkBarrier e => ForkBarrier (rec e)
  | NewLock e => NewLock (rec e)
  | ForkLock e1 e2 => ForkLock (rec e1) (rec e2)
  | Acquire e => Acquire (rec e)
  | Release e1 e2 => Release (rec e1) (rec e2)
  | Wait e => Wait (rec e)
  | Drop e => Drop (rec e)
  end.

Inductive pure_step : expr -> expr -> Prop :=
  | Fun_step x e :
    pure_step (Fun x e) (Val $ FunV x e)
  | App_step x e a :
    pure_step (App (Val $ FunV x e) (Val a)) (subst x a e)
  | Unit_step :
    pure_step Unit (Val $ UnitV)
  | Pair_step v1 v2 :
    pure_step (Pair (Val v1) (Val v2)) (Val $ PairV v1 v2)
  | LetPair_step v1 v2 e:
    pure_step (LetPair (Val $ PairV v1 v2) e) (App (App e (Val v1)) (Val v2))
  | Sum_step n v :
    pure_step (Sum n (Val v)) (Val $ SumV n v)
  | MatchSum_step n (i : fin n) v es :
    pure_step (MatchSum n (Val $ SumV i v) es) (App (es i) (Val v)).

Inductive ctx1 : (expr -> expr) -> Prop :=
  | Ctx_App_l e : ctx1 (λ x, App x e)
  | Ctx_App_r e : ctx1 (λ x, App e x)
  | Ctx_Pair_l e : ctx1 (λ x, Pair x e)
  | Ctx_Pair_r e : ctx1 (λ x, Pair e x)
  | Ctx_LetPair e : ctx1 (λ x, LetPair x e)
  | Ctx_Sum i : ctx1 (λ x, Sum i x)
  | Ctx_MatchSum n es : ctx1 (λ x, MatchSum n x es)
  | Ctx_ForkBarrier : ctx1 (λ x, ForkBarrier x)
  | Ctx_NewLock : ctx1 (λ x, NewLock x)
  | Ctx_ForkLock_l e : ctx1 (λ x, ForkLock x e)
  | Ctx_ForkLock_r e : ctx1 (λ x, ForkLock e x)
  | Ctx_Acquire : ctx1 (λ x, Acquire x)
  | Ctx_Release_l e : ctx1 (λ x, Release x e)
  | Ctx_Release_r e : ctx1 (λ x, Release e x)
  | Ctx_Wait : ctx1 (λ x, Wait x)
  | Ctx_Drop : ctx1 (λ x, Drop x).

Inductive ctx : (expr -> expr) -> Prop :=
  | Ctx_id : ctx id
  | Ctx_comp k1 k2 : ctx1 k1 -> ctx k2 -> ctx (k1 ∘ k2).

Inductive obj := Thread (e : expr) | Barrier | Lock (refcnt : nat) (o : option val).

Definition cfg := gmap nat obj.

Inductive local_step : nat -> cfg -> cfg -> Prop :=

  | Pure_step i k e e' :
    ctx k -> pure_step e e' ->
    local_step i {[ i := Thread (k e) ]} {[ i := Thread (k e') ]}
  | Exit_step i :
    local_step i {[ i := Thread (Val UnitV) ]} ∅

  | Fork_step i j n k v :
    i ≠ j -> i ≠ n -> j ≠ n -> ctx k ->
    local_step i {[ i := Thread (k (ForkBarrier (Val v))) ]}
                 {[ i := Thread (k (Val $ BarrierV n));
                    j := Thread (App (Val v) (Val $ BarrierV n));
                    n := Barrier ]}
  | Sync_step i j n k1 k2 v1 v2 :
    i ≠ j -> i ≠ n -> j ≠ n -> ctx k1 -> ctx k2 ->
    local_step n {[ i := Thread (k1 (App (Val $ BarrierV n) (Val v1)));
                    j := Thread (k2 (App (Val $ BarrierV n) (Val v2)));
                    n := Barrier ]}
                 {[ i := Thread (k1 $ Val v2);
                    j := Thread (k2 $ Val v1) ]}

  | NewLock_step v k n i:
    i ≠ n -> ctx k ->
    local_step i {[ i := Thread (k (NewLock (Val v))) ]}
                 {[ i := Thread (k (Val $ LockV n));
                    n := Lock 0 (Some v) ]}
  | ForkLock_step v o k i j n refcnt :
    i ≠ j -> i ≠ n -> j ≠ n -> ctx k ->
    local_step n {[ i := Thread (k (ForkLock (Val $ LockV n) (Val v)));
                    n := Lock refcnt o ]}
                 {[ i := Thread (k (Val $ LockV n));
                    j := Thread (App (Val v) (Val $ LockV n));
                    n := Lock (S refcnt) o ]}
  | Acquire_step v k i n refcnt :
    i ≠ n -> ctx k ->
    local_step n {[ i := Thread (k (Acquire (Val $ LockV n)));
                    n := Lock refcnt (Some v) ]}
                 {[ i := Thread (k (Val $ PairV (LockV n) v));
                    n := Lock refcnt None ]}
  | Release_step v k i n refcnt :
    i ≠ n -> ctx k ->
    local_step n {[ i := Thread (k (Release (Val $ LockV n) (Val v)));
                    n := Lock refcnt None ]}
                 {[ i := Thread (k (Val $ LockV n));
                    n := Lock refcnt (Some v) ]}
  | Wait_step v k i n :
    i ≠ n -> ctx k ->
    local_step n {[ i := Thread (k (Wait (Val $ LockV n)));
                    n := Lock 0 (Some v) ]}
                 {[ i := Thread (k (Val v)) ]}
  | Drop_step o k i n refcnt :
    i ≠ n -> ctx k ->
    local_step n {[ i := Thread (k (Drop (Val $ LockV n)));
                    n := Lock (S refcnt) o ]}
                 {[ i := Thread (k (Val $ UnitV));
                    n := Lock refcnt o ]}.

Inductive step : nat -> cfg -> cfg -> Prop :=
  | Frame_step ρ ρ' ρf i :
    ρ ##ₘ ρf -> ρ' ##ₘ ρf ->
    local_step i ρ ρ' -> step i (ρ ∪ ρf) (ρ' ∪ ρf).

Definition step' ρ ρ' := ∃ i, step i ρ ρ'.

Definition steps := rtc step'.

         → (l = Unr → env_unr Γ)
           → typed Γ' e t2 → typed Γ (Fun x e) (FunT l t1 t2)

    Var_typed : ∀ (Γ : env) (x : string) (t : type),
                  env_var Γ x t → typed Γ (Var x) t
  | Fun_typed : ∀ (Γ Γ' : env) (x : string) (e : expr)

  | Unit_typed : ∀ Γ : env, env_unr Γ → typed Γ Unit UnitT

  | LetPair_typed : ∀ (Γ Γ1 Γ2 : env) (e1 e2 : expr) (t1 t2 t : type),
                      env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2
                      → typed Γ1 e1 (PairT t1 t2)
                        → typed Γ2 e2 (FunT Lin t1 (FunT Lin t2 t))
                          → typed Γ (LetPair e1 e2) t
  | Sum_typed : ∀ (Γ : env) (n : nat) (ts : fin n → type)

50	  | Release_waiting j v :

From Stdlib Require Import Strings.String.
From cgraphs.locks.lambdalock Require Import definitions.
Open Scope string_scope.

Section Ext.
Context (L : gmap nat type).

Inductive wt : env -> expr -> type -> Prop :=
  | VarW Γ x t :
      env_var Γ x t ->
      wt Γ (Var x) t
  | FunW Γ Γ' x e t1 t2 l :
      env_bind Γ' x t1 Γ ->
      (l = Unr -> env_unr Γ) ->
      wt Γ' e t2 ->
      wt Γ (Fun x e) (FunT l t1 t2)
  | AppW Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t1 t2 l :
      env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
      wt Γ1 e1 (FunT l t1 t2) ->
      wt Γ2 e2 t1 ->
      wt Γ (App e1 e2) t2
  | UnitW Γ :
      env_unr Γ ->
      wt Γ Unit UnitT
  | PairW Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t1 t2 :
      env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
      wt Γ1 e1 t1 ->
      wt Γ2 e2 t2 ->
      wt Γ (Pair e1 e2) (PairT t1 t2)
  | LetPairW Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t1 t2 t :
      env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
      wt Γ1 e1 (PairT t1 t2) ->
      wt Γ2 e2 (FunT Lin t1 (FunT Lin t2 t)) ->
      wt Γ (LetPair e1 e2) t
  | SumW Γ n (ts : fin n -> type) i e :
      wt Γ e (ts i) ->
      wt Γ (Sum i e) (SumT n ts)
  | MatchSumW n Γ Γ1 Γ2 t (ts : fin n -> type) es e :
      env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
      (n = 0 -> env_unr Γ2) ->
      wt Γ1 e (SumT n ts) ->
      (forall i, wt Γ2 (es i) (FunT Lin (ts i) t)) ->
      wt Γ (MatchSum n e es) t
  | ForkW Γ e t1 t2 :
      wt Γ e (FunT Lin (FunT Lin t2 t1) UnitT) ->
      wt Γ (ForkBarrier e) (FunT Lin t1 t2)
  | NewLockW Γ e t :
      wt Γ e t ->
      wt Γ (NewLock e) (LockT (Owner,Closed) t)
  | ForkLockW Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t l1 l2 l3 :
      env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
      lockcap_split l1 l2 l3 ->
      wt Γ1 e1 (LockT l1 t) ->
      wt Γ2 e2 (FunT Lin (LockT l2 t) UnitT) ->
      wt Γ (ForkLock e1 e2) (LockT l3 t)
  | AcquireW Γ e t lo :
      wt Γ e (LockT (lo,Closed) t) ->
      wt Γ (Acquire e) (PairT (LockT (lo,Opened) t) t)
  | ReleaseW Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t lo :
      env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 ->
      wt Γ1 e1 (LockT (lo,Opened) t) ->
      wt Γ2 e2 t ->
      wt Γ (Release e1 e2) (LockT (lo,Closed) t)
  | WaitW Γ e t :
      wt Γ e (LockT (Owner,Closed) t) ->
      wt Γ (Wait e) t
  | DropW Γ e t :
      wt Γ e (LockT (Client,Closed) t) ->
      wt Γ (Drop e) UnitT
  | ValW Γ v t :
      cv L v t ->
      wt Γ (Val v) t
with cv : val -> type -> Prop :=
  | FunVW x e t1 t2 l :

  | UnitVW : cv UnitV UnitT

  | SumVW n (ts : fin n -> type) i v :

  | BarrierVW n t1 t2 :
      cv (BarrierV n) (FunT Lin t1 t2)
  | LockVW n lc t :
      L !! n = Some t ->
      cv (LockV n) (LockT lc t).

End Ext.

(* quick sanity checks *)
Check wt.
Check cv.
EOF

Proof.
  intros H y t Hy. rewrite lookup_delete_Some in Hy. destruct Hy as [Hne Hy]. apply H in Hy. done.

Lemma env_unr_insert_lookup x (t : type) (Γ : env) :

Proof. intros H. apply (H x t). rewrite lookup_insert_eq. done. Qed.

Lemma env_split_empty (Γ1 Γ2 : env) : env_split ∅ Γ1 Γ2 -> Γ1 = ∅ /\ Γ2 = ∅.

  intros [Hun Hdis]. simpl in Hun. symmetry in Hun.
  apply map_positive_l in Hun as H1. apply map_union_comm in Hun. apply map_positive_l in Hun as H2.

  rewrite lookup_delete_Some in H1. rewrite lookup_delete_Some in H2.
  destruct H1 as [Hne1 H1]. destruct H2 as [Hne2 H2]. apply H; done.

  intros Hx. apply map_eq. intro y. destruct (decide (x=y)) as [E|E]; subst.
  - rewrite lookup_delete_eq. done.
  - rewrite lookup_delete_ne by done. rewrite lookup_insert_ne by done. done.

Proof.
  intros Hx. apply map_eq. intro y. destruct (decide (x=y)) as [E|E]; subst.
  - rewrite lookup_delete_eq. done.
  - rewrite lookup_delete_ne by done. done.

Proof.

  - rewrite lookup_insert_eq. rewrite lookup_insert_eq. done.
  - rewrite lookup_insert_ne by done. rewrite lookup_insert_ne by done. done.
Qed.

Lemma insert_insert_comm x y (t1 t2 : type) (Γ : env) : x <> y ->
  <[x:=t1]>(<[y:=t2]>Γ) = <[y:=t2]>(<[x:=t1]>Γ).

  - rewrite lookup_insert_ne by congruence. rewrite lookup_insert_eq. rewrite lookup_insert_eq. done.
  - rewrite lookup_insert_eq. rewrite lookup_insert_eq. rewrite lookup_insert_ne by congruence. done.

    rewrite lookup_insert_ne by congruence. rewrite lookup_insert_ne by congruence. done.
Qed.

Lemma delete_union_eq x (E1 E2 : env) :

Proof.
  intros [Hun Hdis]. split.
  - rewrite delete_union_eq. rewrite <- Hun. done.
  - apply disj_delete. done.
Qed.

Inductive vtyped : val -> type -> Prop :=
  | VUnit : vtyped UnitV UnitT
  | VFun x e t1 t2 l :
      etyped (<[ x := t1 ]> ∅) e t2 ->
      vtyped (FunV x e) (FunT l t1 t2)
  | VPair v1 v2 t1 t2 :
      vtyped v1 t1 -> vtyped v2 t2 -> vtyped (PairV v1 v2) (PairT t1 t2)
  | VSum n i v (ts : fin n -> type) :
      vtyped v (ts i) -> vtyped (SumV i v) (SumT n ts)
with etyped : env -> expr -> type -> Prop :=
  | EVar Γ x t :
      env_var Γ x t -> etyped Γ (Var x) t
  | EFun Γ Γ' x e t1 t2 l :
      env_bind Γ' x t1 Γ ->
      (l = Unr -> env_unr Γ) ->
      etyped Γ' e t2 ->

  | EApp Γ Γ1 Γ2 e1 e2 t1 t2 l :

      etyped Γ1 e1 (FunT l t1 t2) ->
      etyped Γ2 e2 t1 ->

      etyped Γ2 e2 (FunT Lin t1 (FunT Lin t2 t)) ->
      etyped Γ (LetPair e1 e2) t
  | ESum Γ n (ts : fin n -> type) i e :
      etyped Γ e (ts i) -> etyped Γ (Sum i e) (SumT n ts)
  | EMatchSum n Γ Γ1 Γ2 t (ts : fin n -> type) es e :

      etyped Γ1 e (SumT n ts) ->

(* split relation used in the substitution lemma *)
Lemma split_rel Γ E E1 E2 x (t1 : type) :
  Γ !! x = None ->
  (E = <[x:=t1]> Γ \/ E = Γ) ->
  env_split E E1 E2 ->
  env_split Γ (delete x E1) (delete x E2) /\
  (E1 = <[x:=t1]>(delete x E1) \/ E1 = delete x E1) /\
  (E2 = <[x:=t1]>(delete x E2) \/ E2 = delete x E2).
Proof.
  intros Hn [Hrel|Hrel] Hsplit; [| subst E].
  - (* E = insert x t1 Γ *)
    destruct Hsplit as [Hun Hdis].
    (* E1 x and E2 x are None or Some t1 *)
    assert (H1x : E1 !! x = None \/ exists u, E1 !! x = Some u /\ u = t1).
    { destruct (E1 !! x) as [u|] eqn:E1x.
      - right. exists u. split; [done|].
        assert (Ex : E !! x = Some u).
        { rewrite Hun. unfold env. rewrite (lookup_union E1 E2 x). rewrite E1x. done. }
        rewrite Hrel in Ex. rewrite (lookup_insert_eq Γ x t1) in Ex. done.
      - left. done. }
    assert (H2x : E2 !! x = None \/ exists u, E2 !! x = Some u /\ u = t1).
    { destruct (E2 !! x) as [u|] eqn:E2x.
      - right. exists u. split; [done|].
        assert (Ex : E !! x = Some u).
        { rewrite Hun. unfold env. rewrite (lookup_union E1 E2 x). rewrite E2x. done. }
        rewrite Hrel in Ex. rewrite (lookup_insert_eq Γ x t1) in Ex. done.
      - left. done. }
    assert (Hunion : Γ = delete x E1 ∪ delete x E2).
    { rewrite Hrel. rewrite delete_union. rewrite delete_insert_none by done. done. }
    assert (Hdisj : disj (delete x E1) (delete x E2)).
    { apply disj_delete. done. }
    split; [split; assumption|].
    split.
    + destruct H1x as [H1x|[u [H1x Hu]]].
      * right. apply delete_none. done.
      * left. subst u. apply insert_delete_same. done.
    + destruct H2x as [H2x|[u [H2x Hu]]].
      * right. apply delete_none. done.
      * left. subst u. apply insert_delete_same. done.
  - (* E = Γ, x not in E *)
    destruct Hsplit as [Hun Hdis]. subst E.
    assert (H1x : E1 !! x = None).
    { destruct (E1 !! x) as [u|] eqn:E1x; [|done].
      assert (Ex : (Γ) !! x = Some u).

    assert (H2x : E2 !! x = None).

      assert (Ex : (Γ) !! x = Some u).
      { rewrite Hun. unfold env. rewrite (lookup_union E1 E2 x). rewrite E2x. done. }
      rewrite Hn in Ex. done. }
    assert (Hunion : Γ = delete x E1 ∪ delete x E2).
    { rewrite Hun. rewrite delete_union. rewrite delete_none by done. rewrite delete_none by done. done. }
    assert (Hdisj : disj (delete x E1) (delete x E2)).
    { apply disj_delete. done. }
    split; [split; assumption|].
    split; [right; apply delete_none; done|right; apply delete_none; done].
Qed.
EOF

Lemma etyped_var_inv Γ x t : etyped Γ (Var x) t -> env_var Γ x t.

  etyped Γ (App e1 e2) t ->
  exists l t1 t2 Γ1 Γ2, env_split Γ Γ1 Γ2 /\
     etyped Γ1 e1 (FunT l t1 t2) /\ etyped Γ2 e2 t1 /\ t = t2.

Lemma lk_delete (m : E) x y :

Proof. apply lookup_delete. Qed.
Lemma lk_delete_eq (m : E) x : (delete x m) !! x = None.

Lemma lk_delete_ne (m : E) x y : x <> y -> (delete x m) !! y = m !! y.

Proof. intro H. rewrite lk_insert. destruct (decide (x=y)); [done|reflexivity]. Qed.

Proof. intros H. apply map_eq. intro y. rewrite lk_delete.
  destruct (decide (x = y)); [subst; rewrite H; reflexivity|reflexivity]. Qed.

Lemma union_none (m1 m2 : E) x :

Proof. intro H. exact (proj1 (union_none _ _ _ H)). Qed.
Lemma union_none_r (m1 m2 : E) x : (m1 ∪ m2) !! x = None -> m2 !! x = None.
Proof. intro H. exact (proj2 (union_none _ _ _ H)). Qed.

Proof.

content.text:
## 1. Identification

The calculus is a very close match to the Coq artifact accompanying:

> Mako Bates and Joseph P. Near, **“Higher-Order Leak and Deadlock Free Locks”**, PACMPL 7(OOPSLA2), Article 253 (2023).

The distinctive features are all present:
- linear/unrestricted function arrows (`FunT Lin` / `FunT Unr`) with an `unr` predicate and `env_unr`;
- coinductive `type` with `LockT : lockcap -> type -> type`;
- lock capabilities `(Owner|Client, Opened|Closed)`;
- reference-counted lock sharing via `ForkLock`, plus `Acquire`, `Release`, `Wait`, `Drop`;
- `ForkBarrier` with a synchronous barrier/rendezvous value;
- a small-step concurrent semantics over a `gmap nat obj`;
- the notion of `fully_reachable` used for leak- and deadlock-freedom.

I cannot verify the artifact offline, and I cannot recover verbatim helper-lemma names from memory. The theorem name `typed_full_reachability` is plausibly verbatim from the artifact. The proof architecture below is a reconstruction consistent with the definitions and with the paper’s style.

The paper’s soundness argument is essentially:
1. define configuration/heap typing with a linear capability discipline;
2. prove type preservation and progress for runtime configurations;
3. prove the initial configuration is fully reachable;
4. prove full reachability is preserved by reduction;
5. derive leak-freedom and deadlock-freedom as corollaries.

Key paper-level invariants are linear capability accounting, refcount consistency, dual barrier endpoint types, and “no unreferenced/stuck cycle”.

---

## 2. What the local definitions force

Several details of the supplied definitions are essential and easy to miss.

### 2.1 Step indices are sometimes objects, not threads

`local_step : nat -> cfg -> cfg -> Prop` is indexed by a `nat` that is not always a thread id:

- `Pure_step`, `Exit_step`, `Fork_step`, `NewLock_step` use the thread id as index;
- `Sync_step`, `ForkLock_step`, `Acquire_step`, `Release_step`, `Wait_step`, `Drop_step` use the **lock/barrier id** as index.

For example `Sync_step ... : local_step n {[ i := ...; j := ...; n := Barrier ]} ...`, and `Acquire_step ... : local_step n ...`.

Consequently, in

```coq
Definition can_step (ρ : cfg) (i : nat) := ∃ ρ', step i ρ ρ'.
```

a lock `n` is `can_step` exactly when some thread has an enabled lock operation on `n`; a barrier `n` is `can_step` exactly when both endpoints are applied. Threads blocked in a lock/barrier operation are *not* roots; the object is the root. This is central to the reachability proof: a thread `i` at `Acquire (Val (LockV n))` is reachable via `Waiting_reachable i n` once `n` is reachable via `Can_step_reachable n`.

### 2.2 `reachable` is forward reachability in a support graph

Define the support graph `H(ρ)` on live object ids with edges:
- if thread `i` has `expr_waiting e j`, add `j -> i` (wait-support);
- if object `j` references object `i` (`i ∈ obj_refs (ρ!!j)`), and if `ρ!!j` is `Thread e` then `¬ expr_waiting e i`, add `j -> i` (reference-support).

Then

```coq
reachable ρ i
```

is exactly “`i` is forward-reachable in `H(ρ)` from some `can_step` node”. The side condition in the second disjunct of `waiting` is a local 2-cycle guard: a thread that is itself blocked on `i` cannot be used as the reference-witness for `i`.

Also note that `LockV`/`BarrierV` are the only value constructors carrying ids, so `obj_refs` never points to a `Thread`. Threads are reachable only as roots or through the first disjunct of `waiting`; locks/barriers are reachable only as roots or through reference edges.

### 2.3 `expr_head_waiting` includes operations that are currently enabled

`expr_head_waiting` contains `Release`, `Drop`, `ForkLock`, `Acquire`, `Wait`, and barrier application, regardless of whether the operation is enabled. This is deliberate: a thread whose head operation touches `j` should not be usable as the reference-witness for `j` through the second disjunct of `waiting`, even if that operation is currently ready. Otherwise the graph argument would be unsound.

### 2.4 The lock capability algebra is exactly reference counting

For `ForkLock`, `l1` is the capability of the fork operand, `l2` is given to the child, and `l3` is returned to the parent continuation. The splits imply:

- exactly one `Owner` capability per live lock;
- `refcnt` equals the number of `Client` capabilities;
- at most one `Opened` capability; `o = None` iff an `Opened` capability exists;
- `o = Some v` iff all capabilities are `Closed`.

Check the state splits:
- `(Opened, Closed, Opened)`: child gets closed, parent keeps open, object remains `None`;
- `(Opened, Opened, Closed)`: child gets open, parent gets closed, object remains `None`;
- `(Closed, Closed, Closed)`: object remains `Some`.

These transitions match `Acquire` (`Closed -> Opened`, `Some -> None`), `Release` (`Opened -> Closed`, `None -> Some`), `Wait` (`Owner,Closed`, `refcnt = 0`, `Some`, lock destroyed), and `Drop` (`Client,Closed`, `refcnt = S r`, lock remains).

### 2.5 `typed` is source-only; it has no `Val` rule

Every `typed` rule has typed subexpressions, and there is no rule for `Val`. Hence:

> Every `typed Γ e t` contains no `Val` subexpression.

So the initial source `e` has `expr_refs e = ∅`. All runtime `Val` nodes and all concrete `LockV`/`BarrierV` references arise only from pure steps and substitutions. This is why the invariant needs a **runtime typing relation**; the source `typed` relation alone says nothing about runtime configurations.

### 2.6 Linear usage is enforced indirectly

`Var_typed` uses `env_var`, whose other context is `env_unr`; `Unit_typed` requires `env_unr Γ`. Thus a linear variable cannot be silently discarded: any closed typed expression must consume every linear variable. Combined with `env_split`/`disj`, linear variables are used exactly once, and unrestricted variables may be shared.

Consequences:
- pure steps preserve the token multiset (and the set of concrete references) of the acting thread;
- a value substituted for a discarded variable must have `unr` type, and unrestricted values contain no `LockT`/`FunT Lin` tokens;
- `MatchSum` branches share the same linear context, so they contain the same concrete references; dropping unselected branches loses no distinct objects.

### 2.7 Barrier endpoints have no type in the `obj` datatype

`Barrier` carries no payload, and `type` has no barrier constructor. The only consistent runtime typing is:

- one endpoint has type `FunT Lin τ1 τ2`;
- the other has type `FunT Lin τ2 τ1`;
- both are linear (`unr` has no constructor for `FunT Lin`), hence each is used exactly once.

This is exactly what `Fork_typed` produces: from
`e : FunT Lin (FunT Lin t2 t1) UnitT`, the parent gets `FunT Lin t1 t2`, and the child receives the dual `FunT Lin t2 t1`. At `Sync_step` the two values are swapped, which is precisely type-preserving for dual endpoint types. The barrier’s endpoint types must therefore be stored in an auxiliary map in the proof invariant, since the runtime configuration itself does not store them.

## 3. Proposed invariant and proof architecture

A proof of

```coq
Theorem typed_full_reachability e ρ :
  typed ∅ e UnitT -> steps {[ 0 := Thread e ]} ρ -> fully_reachable ρ.
```

should be organized around a configuration invariant `WT ρ` (name is a suggestion) preserved by `step'`, with the initial configuration satisfying it and `WT ρ -> fully_reachable ρ`.

### 3.1 Invariant components

Let `L : gmap nat type` assign payload types to live locks, and `B : gmap nat (type * type)` assign dual endpoint types to live barriers.

Introduce an abstract capability-token type, for example:

```coq
Inductive rtoken :=
| RLock (n : nat) (cap : lockcap)
| RBar  (n : nat) (b : bool).   (* b selects one of the dual endpoint types *)
```

`rtoken` is a countable inductive, so `gmultiset rtoken` is available; do **not** put the coinductive `type` inside the multiset. Payload/endpoint types live in `L`/`B`.

Define `rtyped (Δ : env) (Ξ : gmultiset rtoken) e t`, a runtime typing relation mirroring `typed`, with extra `Val` rules:

- `Val (LockV n)` consumes one `RLock n cap` token and has type `LockT cap t` when `L !! n = Some t`;
- `Val (BarrierV n)` consumes one `RBar n b` token and has type `FunT Lin τ1 τ2` or its dual according to `b` and `B !! n`;
- `Val UnitV`, `Val (PairV ...)`, `Val (SumV ...)`, `Val (FunV x e)` with the obvious rules;
- `Val (FunV x e) : FunT l t1 t2` types the body under `Δ` extended with `x : t1`; if `l = Unr`, the captured context must be unrestricted and `Ξ` must be empty.

The other expression constructors mirror `typed`, splitting `Δ` and `Ξ` linearly.

`WT ρ` should contain:

1. **Thread typing**: for each live thread `i`, `rtyped ∅ Ξ_i e_i UnitT` for some `Ξ_i`.
2. **Stored-value typing**: for each live lock `n` with `ρ!!n = Lock r (Some v)`, `rtyped ∅ Ξ_n v (L!!n)`.
3. **Capability accounting**: the multiset sum of all `Ξ_i` and `Ξ_n` equals the canonical heap multiset determined by `ρ`:
   - for a live lock `n` with state `Lock r (Some v)`: one `Owner` token and `r` `Client` tokens, all `Closed`;
   - for a live lock `n` with state `Lock r None`: one `Owner`, `r` `Client`, exactly one token `Opened`, all others `Closed`;
   - for a live barrier `n`: exactly `RBar n true` and `RBar n false`.
4. **Payload/endpoint consistency**: `L` is defined exactly on live locks; `B` exactly on live barriers; all tokens for `n` use the type assigned by `L`/`B`.
5. **No dangling references**: every ref in a live thread/lock value is live. This follows from 3 plus token typing, but is useful as a derived lemma.
6. **Reachability/support invariant** (the hard part): every live object is supported/ranked so that `fully_reachable ρ` follows. At minimum include `full_reach ρ` itself in `WT`, but the preservation proof needs a stronger structural witness; see Section 5.

The translation of the source derivation to runtime typing is easy:

```coq
Lemma source_rtyped : typed Γ e t -> rtyped Γ ∅ e t.
```

It holds because source `e` has no `Val`; every `typed` rule has a matching `rtyped` rule. For the initial configuration, `Γ = ∅`, so `Ξ = ∅` and `expr_refs e = ∅`.

### 3.2 Overall induction

Use `steps = rtc step'` (`rtc` from stdpp). Prove:

```coq
Lemma WT_init : typed ∅ e UnitT -> WT {[0 := Thread e]}.
Lemma WT_step : WT ρ -> step' ρ ρ' -> WT ρ'.
Lemma WT_full_reachability : WT ρ -> fully_reachable ρ.
```

Then conclude by `rtc_ind` (or `induction` on the `rtc` derivation with a general motive) on `steps {[0 := Thread e]} ρ`.

`step' ρ ρ'` is `∃ i, step i ρ ρ'`; unfold `step` to `Frame_step`, destruct the frame `ρf`, then case-analyse `local_step`. Because the local pre-configuration is a small finite map, the membership of the affected objects is explicit. Freshness of new ids follows from the disjointness hypotheses `ρ ##ₘ ρf` and `ρ' ##ₘ ρf`: if, e.g., `n` is added locally, it cannot be in `ρf`.

### 3.3 Lemmas needed for the typing half

- **Context congruence**: define `ctx_typed` for `ctx1`/`ctx`, with a plug lemma:
  ```coq
  Lemma ctx1_rtyped_plug k Δ Ξ e e' t t' :
    ctx1 k -> rtyped Δ Ξ e t -> rtyped Δ Ξ e' t ->
    rtyped Δ Ξ (k e) t' -> rtyped Δ Ξ (k e') t'.
  ```
  One case per `ctx1` constructor, including the lock/barrier forms and `Ctx_MatchSum`.
- **Pure subject reduction**: for each `pure_step e e'`, if `rtyped Δ Ξ e t` then `rtyped Δ Ξ e' t`.
  - `App_step` needs the substitution lemma:
    ```coq
    Lemma rtyped_subst x a e Δ Ξ_body Ξ_a t1 t2 :
      rtyped (<[x := t1]> Δ) Ξ_body e t2 ->
      rtyped Δ Ξ_a (Val a) t1 ->
      rtyped Δ (Ξ_body ⊎ Ξ_a) (subst x a e) t2.
    ```
    This is the technical heart of the pure cases.
  - `MatchSum_step` uses the fact that every branch is typed with the same resource context `Ξ2`; hence every branch contains the same concrete token ids. Prove a lemma:
    ```coq
    Lemma matchsum_branch_context_eq :
      (∀ j, rtyped Δ2 Ξ2 (es j) _) -> True.
    ```
    More usefully, prove that the concrete reference set of `es i` is the same for every `i`, so the unselected branches can be dropped without losing live references.
  - `Fun_step`, `Unit_step`, `Pair_step`, `LetPair_step`, `Sum_step` are routine.
- **Discarded values are token-free**: if a value has `unr` type, its resource context is empty. This justifies the “unused variable” case of substitution.
- **Token conservation for pure steps**: the multiset `Ξ` is literally unchanged; consequently the set of concrete refs in the thread is unchanged. This is stronger and easier to use than a mere inclusion.

### 3.4 Lemmas needed for capability accounting

- **Lock token transitions**: each lock operation transforms the canonical token multiset exactly as prescribed:
  - `NewLock`: adds one `Owner,Closed` token and moves the initial value’s tokens into the new lock;
  - `ForkLock`: the `lockcap_split` case determines the parent/child token replacement and the refcount increment;
  - `Acquire`: one `Closed` token becomes `Opened`; value tokens move from the lock to the thread;
  - `Release`: one `Opened` token becomes `Closed`; value tokens move from the thread to the lock;
  - `Wait`: only the `Owner,Closed` token exists (`refcnt = 0`); it is consumed and the lock token-set disappears;
  - `Drop`: one `Client,Closed` token is consumed; one `Client` token is removed from the canonical set and `refcnt` decreases.
- **Barrier token transitions**:
  - `Fork_step` creates `RBar n true` and `RBar n false` and assigns the dual types determined by `Fork_typed`;
  - `Sync_step` consumes both tokens and removes `B n`.
- **No dangling refs**: every concrete ref occurrence is a token occurrence; the accounting invariant places every token in a live object’s canonical set; hence all refs point to live objects.
- **No orphan creation**: new objects are always referenced by the creating thread and/or the new child.

## 4. Step-by-step reachability obligations

The following is the case analysis that the preservation proof must perform. It assumes `ρ` is `WT` and fully reachable, and `ρ'` is obtained by one framed local step.

### 4.1 Frame objects

Objects in `ρf` are untouched. Their old reachability witnesses survive unless they depend on the changed thread/object. Since local steps conserve the global token/reference multiset, references to frame objects are moved but not lost. The main work is for the affected thread(s) and the local lock/barrier.

### 4.2 `Pure_step`

- The acting thread’s reference set is exactly preserved (not merely included), by token conservation.
- Other objects/live set unchanged.
- If the thread was a root and ceases to be one, it must be head-waiting on an object in its own expression (e.g. `App (FunV x (Acquire x)) ...` reduces to `Acquire (LockV n)`).
  - If the waited-on lock is unlocked, the lock becomes `can_step` (`Acquire_step` is indexed by the lock).
  - If the lock is locked, the unique `Opened` token is held by another container, which is not a thread waiting on the lock (otherwise the lock would be `can_step` via `Release_step`/`ForkLock_step`); that container supports the lock.
- Therefore the thread remains reachable, and its unchanged reference set supports all objects it supported before.

### 4.3 `Exit_step`

The thread is at `Val UnitV`. Its runtime typing context `Ξ` is empty, so its expression has no concrete references. Removing it cannot orphan a lock/barrier. Threads are never reference targets (`obj_refs` only yields lock/barrier ids), so no `waiting` edge targets the removed thread. Full reachability is unchanged.

### 4.4 `Fork_step`

Pre: `i : Thread (k (ForkBarrier (Val v)))`.
Post: `i : Thread (k (Val (BarrierV n)))`, new `j : Thread (App (Val v) (Val (BarrierV n)))`, new `Barrier n`.

- New barrier `n` is referenced by both `i` and `j`. `B n` is set to `(t1,t2)` from `Fork_typed`, with `i` holding `RBar n true` and `j` holding `RBar n false`.
- `v`’s tokens move from `i` to `j`.
- Reachability of `j`:
  - if `v = FunV ...`, `j` is `can_step` by a pure `App_step`, hence a root;
  - if `v = BarrierV m` (possible because barrier endpoints have function type), `j` is head-waiting on `m`. The other endpoint of `m` is held by some container; if that container is also applying its endpoint, then `m` is `can_step` via `Sync_step`; otherwise that container references `m` and is not waiting on `m`, so it supports `m`. Thus `j` is reachable.
- Since `j` is reachable and references `n` in a non-head position (`n` is the argument of `App`; the head waits on `m` if `v = BarrierV m`, or is a pure redex if `v = FunV`), `n` is reachable.
- `i` then is reachable: either it is still a root, or it is head-waiting on `n` (if its continuation applies the returned endpoint), and `n` is reachable. `i` also references `n` in that case, but support comes from `n`’s can-step/reference witness, not from `i`.

### 4.5 `NewLock_step`

Pre: `i : Thread (k (NewLock (Val v)))`, post: `i : Thread (k (Val (LockV n)))`, new `Lock 0 (Some v)`.

- The new lock has a single `Owner,Closed` token placed in `i`’s continuation.
- `v`’s tokens move into the lock’s stored value.
- `i` was a root and references `n` post. If `i` is not waiting on `n`, then `n` is reachable from `i` by a reference edge. If `i` is waiting on `n` at its head, the fresh lock is unlocked and `i` holds a closed capability, so `n` is `can_step` (`Acquire_step`, `Wait_step`, or `ForkLock_step` as appropriate) and therefore reachable. In either case `n` is reachable, and `v`’s token references are reachable through `n`.

### 4.6 `ForkLock_step`

Pre: `i : Thread (k (ForkLock (Val (LockV n)) (Val v)))`, `n : Lock refcnt o`.
Post: `i : Thread (k (Val (LockV n)))`, new `j : Thread (App (Val v) (Val (LockV n)))`, `n : Lock (S refcnt) o`.

- The `lockcap_split` case determines the token replacement: the old token `RLock n l1` is replaced by `RLock n l3` in `i` and `RLock n l2` in `j`. The refcount increment adds exactly one `Client` token globally.
- `v`’s tokens move from `i` to `j`.
- `i` and `j` both reference `n`.
- `j` is reachable exactly as in `Fork_step`, splitting on whether `v` is a closure or a barrier endpoint.
- `n` is reachable because `j` is reachable and references `n` in the argument position unless `j` is head-waiting on `n`; but `j`’s head is `App (Val v) ...`, where `v` is a function value or barrier endpoint, not a lock operation, so `j` is not waiting on `n` (unless `v` itself references `n` internally, in which case `n` is reached through the function value; the side condition concerns only the head).
- Then `i` is reachable via its continuation, either as a root or by waiting on `n` or another object.

### 4.7 `Acquire_step`

Pre: `i : Thread (k (Acquire (Val (LockV n))))`, `n : Lock refcnt (Some v)`.
Post: `i : Thread (k (Val (PairV (LockV n) v)))`, `n : Lock refcnt None`.

- Token transition: `RLock n (lo,Closed) -> RLock n (lo,Opened)`; `v`’s tokens move from the lock to the thread.
- `n` is still referenced by `i` (the reopened `LockV n` is in the pair).
- If `i` is not head-waiting on `n`, then `n` is reachable from `i`.
- If `i` is head-waiting on `n`, the continuation `k` must accept the result type `PairT (LockT (lo,Opened) t) t`; a well-typed `k` cannot have a head lock operation directly on the pair. Any waiting by `i` is on an object inside the other component of `k` or inside `v`. The newly obtained `Opened` token is the unique opened token for `n`; if `i` is waiting on `n` through a different token from `v`, this is precisely a “two capabilities for the same lock in one thread” situation, which the capability-separation part of `WT` must exclude. Under that invariant, `i`’s wait target is not `n`, and `n` is supported by `i`’s non-head reference.
- The new value tokens of `v` are reachable because they are in `i`’s expression and `i` is reachable.

### 4.8 `Release_step`

Pre: `i : Thread (k (Release (Val (LockV n)) (Val v)))`, `n : Lock refcnt None`.
Post: `i : Thread (k (Val (LockV n)))`, `n : Lock refcnt (Some v)`.

- Token transition: `RLock n (lo,Opened) -> RLock n (lo,Closed)`; `v`’s tokens move from the thread to the lock.
- `n` is referenced by `i` post. If `i` is head-waiting on `n` (e.g. its continuation is `Wait`), then:
  - if `refcnt = 0`, `n` is `can_step` via `Wait_step` (or `ForkLock_step`), hence reachable;
  - if `refcnt > 0`, the client tokens are held elsewhere. A client container cannot be a thread waiting on `n` in an enabled head operation (with `o = Some`, `Acquire`, `Drop`, and `ForkLock` are enabled, and `Release` requires `o = None`), so a client container supports `n`. Thus `n` is reachable, and then `i` is reachable via waiting.
- The stored value’s references are reachable through `n` once `n` is reachable.

### 4.9 `Wait_step`

Pre: `i : Thread (k (Wait (Val (LockV n))))`, `n : Lock 0 (Some v)`.
Post: `i : Thread (k (Val v))`, lock `n` removed.

- The owner token is the only token for `n` (`refcnt = 0`). It is consumed; the lock disappears.
- Token accounting guarantees there are no other references to `n`: every concrete `LockV n` occurrence would be a token, and the only token was the owner’s operand. Hence removing `n` creates no dangling reference.
- `v`’s tokens move to `i`; `i` is reachable by the usual support argument (it was a root pre-step; if it becomes blocked, its new head object is supported).
- References inside `v` that were previously supported by `n` are now supported by `i`; if `i` is itself waiting on one of them, the capability state of that object supplies a different holder (the same support lemma as above).

### 4.10 `Drop_step`

Pre: `i : Thread (k (Drop (Val (LockV n))))`, `n : Lock (S refcnt) o`.
Post: `i : Thread (k (Val UnitV))`, `n : Lock refcnt o`.

- One `Client,Closed` token is consumed; the canonical token set loses exactly one client; the lock remains live.
- `i` loses its reference to `n`, but `n` still has its unique `Owner` token (and possibly other clients), so it remains referenced by some live container. Since the owner token holder is not the dropped client, `n` does not become unreachable.
- `i` is reachable as a root or via its continuation; its expression now has no reference to `n`.

### 4.11 `Sync_step` (the delicate case)

Pre:
```
i : Thread (k1 (App (Val (BarrierV n)) (Val v1)))
j : Thread (k2 (App (Val (BarrierV n)) (Val v2)))
n : Barrier
```
Post:
```
i : Thread (k1 (Val v2))
j : Thread (k2 (Val v1))
```
and `n` is removed.

Facts to use:

1. **Root/reachability pre**: the barrier `n` is `can_step` because `Sync_step` is indexed by `n`. Hence both `i` and `j` are reachable pre via the first disjunct of `waiting` on `n`.

2. **Barrier typing**: `B n = (t1,t2)`. One endpoint token is `RBar n true` with type `FunT Lin t1 t2`; the other is `RBar n false` with type `FunT Lin t2 t1`. Both are linear, so exactly two occurrences exist.
   - If `i` holds `RBar n true` and `j` holds `RBar n false`, then:
     - `i`’s `App` types `v1 : t1` and yields `v2 : t2`;
     - `j`’s `App` types `v2 : t2` and yields `v1 : t1`.
   - If the orientations are reversed, the roles of `t1`/`t2` and `v1`/`v2` are swapped.
   The runtime typing invariant records which orientation each thread holds; the proof must case-split on this.

3. **Typing post**:
   - `i`’s post expression `k1 (Val v2)` is typed with `Ξ_{k1} ⊎ Ξ_{v2}`;
   - `j`’s post expression `k2 (Val v1)` is typed with `Ξ_{k2} ⊎ Ξ_{v1}`.
   This is exactly the pre contexts with the barrier token removed and the two value contexts swapped.

4. **Token accounting post**: the two `RBar n` tokens are consumed, `B n` is removed, and the value token multisets `Ξ_{v1}`, `Ξ_{v2}` are swapped between `i` and `j`. The global token multiset loses exactly the barrier tokens; the canonical heap loses exactly the barrier.

5. **No dangling**: the only two concrete `BarrierV n` occurrences pre are the two endpoint operands at the heads of `i` and `j`; linearity forbids any other occurrence. They are consumed, so no reference to the removed barrier remains.

6. **Reachability post**:
   - `i` is either `can_step` post (if `k1 (Val v2)` has a pure redex/exit/fork/newlock redex) or head-waiting on some lock/barrier `m` in `k1` or in `v2`.
   - `m` was already reachable pre: `v2` was referenced by `j` pre, and `j` was reachable and was head-waiting on `n`, so the reference edge `j -> m` was valid for `m ≠ n`; `k1`’s references were referenced by `i` pre.
   - If `m`’s pre reachability witness used the fact that `j` referenced it via `v2`, then post `j` no longer contains `v2`; however `i` now contains `v2`. If `i` is waiting on `m`, the side condition prevents `i` from supporting `m`; in that case the capability-state argument supplies another holder of `m`:
     - if `m` is a lock and `i` is blocked acquiring it, the unique `Opened` token is held by another container not waiting on `m`;
     - if `m` is a barrier and `i` is blocked on it, the other endpoint is held by a container not applying it (otherwise `m` would be `can_step` and would support `i` directly).
   - Symmetrically for `j`.

This is the case where the dual barrier types and the capability/refcount invariants interact most tightly. A proof that only tracks `expr_refs` and the syntactic swap is not enough; the post-step support of swapped values needs the capability-state facts.

## 5. The reachability half: the hard global invariant

The local definitions give a clean picture but not a complete proof. The difficult part is the global “no stuck/leaked cycle” invariant. The following is the most plausible reconstruction of the paper’s argument and the shape a Coq proof would need.

### 5.1 Support lemma for blocked operations

Prove a lemma of roughly this form:

> If `WT ρ`, thread `i` is live, `expr_waiting e_i j`, and `i` is not `can_step`, then either `can_step ρ j`, or there is a live container `z` such that `j ∈ obj_refs (ρ!!z)`, `z` is not a thread waiting on `j`, and `z` is already known reachable (e.g. by the induction hypothesis from the pre-state).

Case analysis on the head operation:
- `Acquire` blocked: the lock is `None`; exactly one `Opened` token exists and is held by another container. A thread holding an `Opened` token cannot be head-waiting on the same lock in a stuck state: `Release` and `ForkLock` would be enabled, and `Acquire`/`Wait`/`Drop` require incompatible capabilities.
- `Wait` blocked: either `o = None` (use the `Opened` token holder) or `refcnt > 0` (use a `Client` token holder; with `o = Some`, the client’s enabled operations would make the lock `can_step` unless the client is blocked elsewhere, so its reference is a valid non-waiting support).
- Barrier application blocked: not both endpoints are applied; the other endpoint holder is not applying its endpoint (otherwise `Sync_step` is enabled), so it is a valid non-waiting support.

This lemma is the local engine that turns capability accounting into reachability.

### 5.2 Acyclicity / distinguished-token support graph

The side condition in `waiting` only forbids 2-cycles. To conclude global reachability, the proof needs a well-founded support structure. Two viable Coq formulations:

**(A) Distinguished-token forest.** Use only one distinguished token per object:
- for a lock `n`, the unique `Owner` token;
- for a barrier `n`, the two endpoint tokens.

Each distinguished token is held by exactly one container (thread or lock value). Define edges from a container to the objects it references, and from an object to a waiter (the `waiting` edge). Show this support graph is acyclic and every live node reaches a `can_step` node. Acyclicity should follow from the way capabilities can be created and moved:
- a new token is created only at `NewLock`, `ForkLock`, or `ForkBarrier`;
- a capability can be stored into a lock only by a thread that holds an `Opened` key capability for that lock, and after the `Release` the thread still holds a `Closed` key capability;
- hence each “stored capability” edge can be charged to a still-live key holder, giving a well-founded parent relation.
This is the natural formal counterpart of the paper’s deadlock-freedom argument. It is also the part most likely to require substantial auxiliary invariants (for example, a “capability separation” or “token locations form a forest” predicate) to exclude a thread holding two complementary capabilities of the same lock, or both endpoints of the same barrier.

**(B) Explicit reachability ranking.** Maintain, as a ghost component of `WT`, a map `rank : nat -> nat` on live objects such that for every live `x`:
- `can_step ρ x`, or
- there exists `y` with `waiting ρ x y` and `rank y < rank x`.
Then `reachable ρ x` follows by induction on `rank x` (the `waiting` derivation gives reachability of the smaller-ranked support). Preserving such a rank through a step requires re-ranking only the affected objects and the moved value subtrees; acyclicity of the support graph is exactly what makes this possible. This is a clean Coq induction principle but still needs the acyclicity input.

A third formulation, likely closest to the paper, is a **logical relation / semantic typing** in which the interpretation of `LockT` and barrier endpoint types includes “the corresponding object is reachable”, and the fundamental theorem gives `typed ∅ e UnitT` implies the initial thread and all objects it spawns are reachable. The syntactic invariant route is more concrete; the logical-relation route is more robust but heavier.
